keyframe_review.note: 463,074 km2 for 1990-2023 against the infobox 455,503 km2 (ratio 1.017): the union of North Yemen and South Yemen as one outline, on a raster whose bounding box (42.0-54.5 E, 12.3-18.9 N) reaches Socotra, which the page says 'belong to Yemen'. The shape is the whole state; the 2014 split between Houthi-held north, Aden and Marib is carried by the ledger's contest events, not by this keyframe. The page dates the unification 22 May 1990 and the border treaty with Saudi Arabia to summer 2000; neither moves the shape. Cliopatria also gives its Wikipedia title 'Yemen' but the Wikidata id Q199841 it shares with the South Yemen row.

Identical to 1990-2023 (463,074 km2). The war page records no recognised change of frontier in 2024; the Houthis 'currently control the capital Sanaa and all of former North Yemen except for eastern Marib Governorate', which the contest event draws, and the STC offensive of December 2025 falls after the map's last year.

region.text: North and South Yemen as one state

ledger.note: 1990: North and South Yemen unite as the Republic of Yemen. 'The countries were merged on 22 May 1990, with Saleh as president' (the Yemen Arab Republic of 1962 in the north, the People's Democratic Republic of Yemen independent since 1967 in the south).
1990: the Yemen Arab Republic (North Yemen) enters the union; its dossier ends the same day.

region.text: the People's Democratic Republic of Yemen (South Yemen)

ledger.note: 1990: South Yemen enters the union; its dossier ends the same day.

region.text: all of former North Yemen except eastern Marib Governorate, with Sanaa

ledger.note: 2014: the Houthis seize Sanaa and the civil war begins. The war page dates the war from 16 September 2014 and has Houthi fighters take Sanaa after a battle lasting only a few days; the Yemen page has the insurgency (begun June 2004) escalating in September 2014 'as anti-government forces led by Abdul-Malik al-Houthi swept into the capital'. The zone is the page's present-day snapshot ('all of former North Yemen except for eastern Marib Governorate'), which is undated; the extent held in 2014 itself is not on the page. Still unpaired in 2024: the contest has no end by then.

2015: the government flees Sanaa for Aden. Hadi 'managed to flee from Sanaa to Aden' on 21 February 2015 and 'declared Aden Yemen's "temporary" capital'; Sanaa stays the constitutional capital under Houthi rule. On 25 March the Houthis reached Aden's outskirts (war page) and Hadi left the country; the pages opened do not say when they were driven back.

2018: the Southern Transitional Council seizes Aden. 'In February 2018, Aden was seized by the UAE-backed separatist Southern Transitional Council.' Unpaired within the map's years: the war page has the STC controlling 90-95% of the populated areas of former South Yemen by 9 December 2025 and dissolving on 9 January 2026, both after 2024.

wars.name: 1994 civil war in Yemen
belligerents: southern leaders (as the page words it)
wars.outcome: The page says only that an accord between northern and southern leaders signed in Amman on 20 February 1994 'could not stop the civil war'; it is silent on the secession of the south, the winner and the fall of Aden. Cliopatria's single 1990-2023 shape implies the unified state survived.
wars.note: A secession dossier (the south's 1994 'Democratic Republic of Yemen') is not on any page I opened; see notes.

wars.name: Houthi insurgency in Yemen
wars.outcome: 'The Houthi insurgency in Yemen began in June 2004', escalating in September 2014 when the Houthis swept into the capital and the civil war began.
wars.note: The page names no province for the 2004 insurgency, so no zone is given.

wars.name: Yemeni civil war (2014-present)

zones.text: all of former North Yemen except eastern Marib Governorate, with Sanaa

wars.outcome: Ongoing at 2024. The Houthis hold Sanaa and all of former North Yemen except eastern Marib; the Presidential Leadership Council is the UN-recognised government; the STC held Aden from 2018. A UN truce took effect on 2 April 2022 (extended on 2 June 2022, officially expired in October).
wars.note: Dates of the war page: Aden Airport lost by pro-Hadi troops on 19 March 2015; Houthis took Lahij and reached Aden on 25 March 2015 when Hadi fled the country. Not on the page: the loss of the south in July 2015, the Stockholm Agreement, the Marib offensive.

wars.name: Saudi-led intervention in Yemen
wars.outcome: 'On 26 March 2015, Saudi Arabia announced Operation Decisive Storm', the start of the airstrikes; no change of frontier is recorded by the pages opened.
wars.note: The war page describes no Houthi ground occupation of Saudi territory, only strikes on Jizan, Najran and Abha in 2026.

certainty.note: No border treaty is recorded on the Yemen page before the summer 2000 Saudi treaty; the Oman frontier (the page is silent on a 1992 agreement) and the Hanish Islands dispute with Eritrea (page silent) were not checked.
'Yemen and Saudi Arabia signed an International Border Treaty' in summer 2000. Exceptions: the front lines since 2014 (Houthi north, Marib, Aden) are not borders and are drawn by contest events.

notes: Pages used: 2 (the budget is 1-2). Rows: Cliopatria gives this row Wikidata Q199841, the same id as the People's Democratic Republic of Yemen (Wikipedia title 'South Yemen'); the two are different states (the republic is the union of North and South Yemen on 22 May 1990, per the Yemen page), so this is its own dossier with both as predecessors (north-yemen already names it as successor) and the shared id looks like a Cliopatria mistake. Not settled: (1) the 1994 civil war: the Yemen page has the Amman accord of 20 February 1994 failing and is silent on the south's secession (a 'Democratic Republic of Yemen' declared in May 1994 would be a rebel state of seven weeks; I did not open a page for it, so no dossier or contest is recorded) and the war's end; (2) the extent of Houthi control in 2014-2015 year by year (the war page gives only the present snapshot, an advance on Aden on 25 March 2015 and no date for the retreat), so the Houthi contest is drawn as the present zone from 2014 at confidence 2; (3) the Tihama coast, Hodeidah (2018 Stockholm Agreement) and Marib (2020-2021) are not on the pages; (4) 2025-2026 on the war page (STC offensive 2-9 December 2025, its defeat and dissolution by 9 January 2026, Houthi gains on the Red Sea coast in September 2026) falls after the map's last year and is not in the ledger; (5) Socotra and the Hanish Islands: the page says Socotra belongs to Yemen and is silent on the Hanish dispute. Counterparts needing dossiers: houthis (Ansar Allah, Supreme Political Council, rebel, 2014-), southern-transitional-council (2017-2026). Gazetteer names used: all resolve.
